name: model-scan
title: Model Scan
description: A photo becoming a 3D character, driven by an engine's events through props: landmark groups light up over the photo as meshes while the background dims around the person (from the engine's mask, or a hull around the pose landmarks), the person's pixels fly as a point cloud onto the base model while the camera turns, a shimmer reveals it and a pulse runs across the floor, streamed weights reshape it, and it hands over to orbit. Floating glass controls follow the stage: a style picker and Make 3D, a progress ring with Cancel, a toolbar of views, the clip, Download and Start over, and the error with Try again. Reduced motion crossfades instead. Announces each stage; agents get start, cancel, retry, restart and download.
docs: `<ModelScan src alt width height stage points masks model weights scaledWeights targetNames expressions progress statusText error onStart onCancel onRetry onStartOver onDownload styles selectedStyle onStyleChange controls modelAlt idleClip aspectRatio fit viewer actions labels>`: `stage` is `photo`, `detecting`, `building`, `refining`, `ready` or `error`: the UI's, which you map from your engine's. `points` light up while detecting: one list (a Float32Array of interleaved x, y fractions of the original photo, or `{ x, y }` objects), or groups `{ source, points, aspect?, edges? }` (the face, the body) that each light up on their own, in the order their sources arrived, a later group replacing its source's; `edges` (pairs of point indices) join a group into a mesh, and a `body` group of the 33 pose landmarks has the pose skeleton by default. They land straight on the photo where the stage draws it, following `fit` (`contain`, or `cover` in a stage of another `aspectRatio`); points past 0 or 1 are kept but not drawn. `masks` are the engine's person masks, `{ source?: "face" | "body", width, height, data }` (`data` a Uint8Array of 0-255 confidence, row-major from the top left, the photo's aspect): the body mask, or one of the photo's aspect, dims the background around the person while detecting and picks the pixels that fly onto the model; without one, a hull around the body's 33 pose landmarks stands in, and without those every pixel flies. `model` is the base GLB with morph targets, from `building` on: a URL, its bytes, or `{ glb, targetNames }`; the final character fades in over it keeping the weights. `weights` and `expressions` ease as they stream. At `building` the photo moves into the 3D scene exactly where the 2D photo was, then the person's pixels fly on curved, staggered paths onto points sampled over the model's surface, turning the info colour mid-flight and the surface's own as they land, a shimmer runs down the body revealing the model, the background's pixels drift out of focus, and a pulse runs across the floor, while the camera turns to the three-quarter view: one draw call, uniforms per frame. Under reduced motion the photo crossfades into the model. The controls float over the stage (`controls="overlay"`, the default) or sit under it (`"below"`): over the photo the style picker (`styles` of `{ value, label }`, `selectedStyle`, `onStyleChange`) and Make 3D (`onStart`); while working a progress ring, the stage's label (`statusText`), Step n of 4, the percent and Cancel (`onCancel`); over the finished model the style picker and a toolbar of views, the clip (`labels.play`), Download (`onDownload`) and Start over (`onStartOver`), icon buttons with tooltips; at `error` the message (`error`) with Try again (`onRetry`) and Start over. Each shows only with its callback; `actions` adds your own. All copy is in `labels`. The model's viewer takes drag and keys without a bar of its own (pass more of its props through `viewer`, like `floor={false}`). Screen readers hear each stage, progress at most every tenth and two seconds, and the error at once. Agents call `start`, `cancel`, `retry`, `restart` and `download`; a call the stage doesn't offer, or the app refuses through `details.cancel()`, fails the step with why.
